title: Error patterns in the cross-tangled-finger illusion under visual and tactile cueing
abstract: The cross-tangled-finger illusion occurs when observers view their crossed wrists and interlaced fingers and attempt to raise a visually indicated finger but instead raise another. We quantified response errors under visual and tactile cueing. Tactile cueing sharply reduced errors. Under visual cueing, raising the corresponding digit on the opposite hand was the most frequent error. Nevertheless, different-digit errors accompanied 31% of opposite-hand responses but only 3% of correct-hand responses, suggesting an association between hand-laterality and digit-identity errors.
